Lichen planus

Both groups improved in a 2024 trial, with no between-group difference, while a 2026 trial reported greater short-term pain and clinical-score improvement with red-light PBM than with topical triamcinolone.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Both groups improved in a 2024 trial, with no between-group difference, while a 2026 trial reported greater short-term pain and clinical-score improvement with red-light PBM than with topical triamcinolone.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Oral > Lichen planus category contains 36 unique titles, including 24 human clinical publications, 10 systematic reviews, six meta-analyses, one narrative review, one protocol, and one cost analysis. Review and meta-analysis labels overlap with publication types, and reviews synthesize trials already counted rather than adding patient cohorts.

Human and clinical evidence

Randomized trials make up much of the clinical record, but they test different forms of oral lichen planus and different comparators. In a 44-person trial of erosive disease, 980-nm near-infrared diode PBM and topical triamcinolone both reduced pain and lesion scores, with no significant difference between groups (Mohamed et al. 2024). A 2026 single-blind trial randomized 60 people with symptomatic disease to red-light PBM or topical corticosteroid. The PBM group had greater improvement in pain and clinical signs over the four-week treatment and short follow-up (Hemanth et al. 2026). These results do not establish long-term control or replacement of standard care.

Animal evidence

No relevant animal study was identified in the exact indication category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell, tissue, or ex-vivo study was identified for this indication.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 2024 trial used a 980-nm near-infrared diode laser at 300 mW, twice weekly for five weeks. The 2026 trial used a 660-nm red diode laser at 4 J/cm² three times weekly for four weeks. These protocols differ in wavelength, schedule, and clinical population. Other records use additional settings, so the results do not identify one transferable dose.

Interpretation

The evidence supports short-term symptom and lesion improvement with some PBM regimens, while comparative benefit over corticosteroids remains inconsistent. The large number of reviews reflects a broad research literature, not the same number of independent patient cohorts.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for short-term lesion and symptom improvement in oral lichen planus
Publications and records36 unique titles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The rating reflects 12 randomized trials but does not assume those publications represent 12 independent, well-powered replications. Direct trials compare different red or near-infrared schedules with steroid care, and findings range from similar to better short-term symptom scores. Larger sham-controlled trials with prespecified lesion and pain outcomes and follow-up beyond treatment would clarify durability.
